changelog._extraSurfacesNote: The served copy here had gone FIVE MONTHS stale before it was caught, because nothing read it: no build, test or check touched public/CHANGELOG.md. That is the specific incident this check exists to prevent recurring.

extraSurfaces.note: Served copy. Keep byte-identical — copy the root file, do not hand-edit both.
In-app changelog. Uses double quotes throughout; the default pattern accepts either.

_claudeMdNote: Deliberately empty. Swept on 2026-07-30: CLAUDE.md contains 21 lines carrying an X.Y.Z string, and every one is historical prose in the Key Files table — '(v0.59.0)', '(v0.49.0)', 're-synced v0.57.4'. Those are correct as written and must never be flagged. There is no `Current Version` / `Live facts` style declaration line to check. If one is ever added, add its pattern here. (MyScrumBudget shipped a guard that matched only one of its two declarations and missed a stale second one — sweep the whole file for X.Y.Z before assuming, and note that `\b\d` will not match `v0.59.0`.) The '1719 tests across 83 test files' claim in Testing Patterns is a COUNT, not a version, so it cannot be machine-checked against package.json — update it by hand.

commands.name: lint
commands._note: eslint exits NON-ZERO here and that is correct — gate on the NUMBER not moving, never on the exit code. `expectProblems` above is the single source of truth for the accepted baseline; it is deliberately the only place the count is written, so there is no second copy to go stale. Re-derive it from `npm run lint` immediately before each commit and set it in the same commit. The baseline is mostly sonarjs/cognitive-complexity on core scheduling and simulation functions, plus react-hooks/set-state-in-effect. William confirmed it as accepted; do NOT refactor those functions merely to satisfy the threshold. The ratchet fails in BOTH directions — if problems were resolved, lower it.

commands.name: build (tsc -b && vite build)
commands._note: `tsc -b` covers test files here — tsconfig.app.json includes src/**/*.ts, and injecting an error into a .test.ts was verified to fail the build. So no separate typecheck step is needed, unlike MyScrumBudget where `next build` skipped tests entirely.

_contractHashNote: `npm run contract:hash` is deliberately NOT a gate step. It PRINTS the digest and exits 0 whatever it finds, so as a command it would be a guard-shaped no-op — it only ever helped when a human ran it in both repos and compared by eye. The real assertion now lives in src/integration/ai-op-contract-hash.test.ts, which pins the digest and therefore runs in the always-true tier. The script stays for the two-repo comparison workflow.
